items.title: Why MAGA Really Hates Fauci
items.description: H alf a dozen years ago, Anthony Fauci was as popular as he would ever be. A respected physician and researcher for decades, he became in 2020 the public face of the pandemic response—calm, confident, and reassuring, a symbol of scientific authority. And the country turned him into a folk hero. He was on the cover of Time , named one of People magazine’s People of the Year, and played by Brad Pitt on Saturday Night Live . Vendors sold Fauci votive candles and bobbleheads. In April of that year, Kim Kardashian convened three dozen movie stars and athletes on a private video call so he could talk to them about masks and crowds—an hour of his time, he later explained, to reach millions of their fans. Then it all came apart. Last week, Fauci testified before the Senate Committee on Homeland Security and Governmental Affairs, chaired by Senator Rand Paul—a fierce Fauci critic who has said that the American people want the 85-year-old retired scientist “behind bars.” Acting on his lawyer’s advice, Fauci invoked his Fifth Amendment right against self-incrimination more than 100 times, citing what he called Paul’s “unhinged obsession” with him. Yesterday, the committee voted along party lines to hold Fauci in contempt of Congress for refusing to answer questions. The hearing produced an avalanche of ad hominem attacks , ludicrous claims , and accusations—most of them years old and long since answered. But two matter more than the rest, because so much of Paul’s case rests on them: (1) that Fauci funded the research that made the pandemic, and (2) that he lied to Congress about it. Fauci ran the National Institute of Allergy and Infectious Diseases, an arm of the National Institutes of Health that hands out several billion dollars a year in research grants. One of those grants went to a New York nonprofit, EcoHealth Alliance, which over five years passed a total of about $600,000 to a Wuhan, China, lab studying bat coronaviruses. NIAID awards thousands of grants a year; NIH staff signed off on the Wuhan lab as a subrecipient, and an institute director does not personally review such arrangements. More important, the bat viruses that the grant paid the lab to study are so genetically distant from SARS-CoV-2 that they could not have produced it, a point that independent virologists have made repeatedly. That disposes of the specific charge that research that Fauci’s agency funded produced the virus. It did not. A s for the origins of the virus itself, nobody has established with certainty where the pandemic began. Chinese stonewalling means that we are unlikely to ever know. No outside investigator has been given the Wuhan Institute of Virology’s records, its early samples, or the medical files of its staff. However, the scientific evidence favors a natural origin. This includes epidemiological evidence showing that the first COVID-19 cases clustered around one corner of Wuhan’s Huanan Seafood Wholesale Market, where wild animals were being butchered. Environmental samples taken from that same area of the market contain , in the same swab, the SARS-CoV-2 sequence and DNA from potential intermediate hosts such as the raccoon dog. The accusation that Fauci lied to Congress rests on his denial, in a 2021 exchange with Paul, that NIH had ever funded gain-of-function research at the Wuhan lab. The point of such research is to learn what a virus would need to jump into humans before it does, so that vaccines and treatments can be ready. [ Read: Lab-leak payback has begun ] The trouble is the term gain of function . In biology, it means research that gives an organism a new capability—engineering a bacterium to digest an oil spill is gain-of-function research. In politics, it has come to mean something narrower and more alarming: deliberately making a dangerous virus more dangerous. Federal rules use a third definition, narrower still. The federal framework adopted in 2017, after years of public debate, covers work to enhance a pathogen that is “likely highly transmissible and likely capable of wide and uncontrollable spread in human populations” and “likely highly virulent and likely to cause significant morbidity and/or mortality in humans.” It also excludes viruses, however dangerous, as they exist in nature. (The policy was revised in 2024.) The gap between those definitions is the whole dispute, and it is why the perjury charge fails twice over. Fauci says that in 2021, he was answering Paul by using the regulatory definition of gain of function —the one that determines what NIH may and may not fund, and the only one that his answer was actually about. By that standard, NIH had reviewed the grant to the Wuhan lab before funding it and had concluded that the research fell outside the framework, on the grounds that the lab was studying wild-collected bat viruses that were not expected to produce severe disease in people. The two men meant different things by the same phrase. And even if you set that aside, perjury requires a knowingly false statement. Five years later, there’s still no evidence that Fauci said anything he believed to be untrue. W hat was new last week was the discovery of a diary. Fauci kept one throughout the pandemic, and Paul—working with Robert F. Kennedy Jr.’s Department of Health and Human Services, which located the files on a government server—released more than 1,100 pages of it, in entries spanning from December 2019 through Fauci’s retirement, in December 2022. Paul posted on X about Fauci, “What he wrote privately and what he told the country are two different stories.” But two analyses—one by FactCheck.org , the other by PolitiFact —show that in the entries Paul highlighted, Fauci’s private notes did not substantially differ from his public statements. The senator from Kentucky has been at this for six years now, pursuing a man who led his institute for 38 years, who advised seven presidents, and whose work has saved countless lives. Accusing him of crimes and deception wasn’t enough; the release of the diary was meant to inflict public humiliation on him. And to some degree, it worked. Fauci was swept up in his own celebrity—starstruck by the famous, thrilled by his invitations to A-list parties, keeping a running tally of his appearances in the press. It was not a good look. But this thought occurred to me as well: If three years’ worth and 1,000 pages of your diary were published tomorrow, how would you fare? Most of us would count ourselves relieved if the worst they revealed was that we had been dazzled by Hollywood stars and flattered when they called. And nowhere in his diary did Fauci confess to paying hush money to a porn star or brag that when you’re famous, you can “grab ’em by the pussy.” A nthony Fauci spent five decades at NIH treating diseases that most often kill the poor, the weak, and the marginalized. He developed highly effective therapies that made once-fatal autoimmune conditions survivable before most Americans had heard of him. In the 1980s, he took AIDS in America seriously when many in the federal government wouldn’t. He met with, and later became friends with, Larry Kramer, an AIDS activist who had called him a “ murderer .” Fauci then spearheaded a major shift that allowed patients far greater access to experimental drugs. Two decades into the epidemic, as AIDS was killing millions in the world’s poorest countries, he was a key architect of PEPFAR—the emergency plan that President George W. Bush launched in 2003 that provided funding and medical resources to combat the global HIV/AIDS epidemic. It is estimated to have saved more than 25 million lives, most of them in sub-Saharan Africa. When anthrax spores arrived in the mail in the weeks after the 9/11 attacks, Fauci led the federal research response and laid the foundations of the biodefense system that we still rely on. He was also central to the development of mRNA vaccines . In the 1990s, he helped persuade President Bill Clinton to fund the NIH Vaccine Research Center, then recruited world-class scientists to staff it. One of them was studying mRNA as a platform for a MERS vaccine when the pandemic began. Because that expertise was already in place, the design for the protein that the COVID mRNA vaccine would use was finished within 48 hours of the viral genome being published. Within roughly 11 months, the first vaccine was authorized for use. The Commonwealth Fund estimates that more than 3.2 million lives were saved as a result of the vaccination program in America from December 2020 to November 2022. The development of mRNA vaccines for COVID was a stunning medical achievement. In 2014, Fauci managed and directed the funding for research for an Ebola vaccine. When a Dallas nurse caught the virus while she cared for a dying man, Fauci put on protective gear and went into the isolation room himself. Eight days later, he walked the nurse out in public and hugged her. This is the man whom Paul, Kennedy, Elon Musk, Joe Rogan, Republicans in Congress, the MAGA movement, and Donald Trump have decided to defame and vilify , and are intent on destroying? [ David Frum: Anthony Fauci is not the villain in this story ] So what explains the rage directed at one of the most distinguished scientists of his generation? Some of it is the result of an era in which a major political party—in this case, the Republican Party—has become deranged and captive to conspiratorial thinking. It draws energy from the dark passions. Many people within the party, especially within its leadership and the right-wing ecosystem, delight in destroying institutions and individuals. Fauci has a target on his back because during the pandemic, he refused to live in the Twilight Zone. He called out those who did. And for MAGA world, that is unforgivable. Some of the fury aimed at Fauci may also be unprocessed grief and anger about the pandemic and its painful memories. My colleague David Brooks, then at The New York Times , wrote in 2020 that pandemics—unlike some other natural catastrophes—tend to drive people apart. In the aftermath of pandemics, people either try to forget them or find others to blame for them. Viruses can’t be punished; people can. Attributing the pandemic to fate or random chance isn’t all that satisfying; a lot of people need a villain, even if, in this case, the villain is one of the men who helped end the pandemic that was ravaging the world. In Albert Camus’ The Plague , the protagonist, Dr. Bernard Rieux, is an admirable if imperfect character. When others flee Oran, he stays. He works until he’s exhausted, even while knowing that many will die. An atheist and a humanist, he ultimately stands with victims, finding meaning through helping others. He doesn’t think of himself as a hero so much as a decent man doing his job. Neither does he pretend to understand suffering; instead, he fights against it. He is one of the “true healers.” At the conclusion of the novel, Rieux concludes that plagues ultimately teach us that “there are more things to admire in men than to despise.” There is much more to admire in Anthony Fauci than to despise. The same cannot be said of many of his critics.

items.title: What Mitch McConnell Did
items.description: O n the first Saturday of every August, the Saint Jerome Catholic Church in the tiny town of Fancy Farm, Kentucky, hosts a picnic renowned for its mutton-and-pork barbecue. Since 1880, the scent of smoked meat has attracted people; the whiff of votes then attracted politicians. The picnic long ago morphed into the premier event in the state’s campaign season, attracting its most famous officeholders. As attendees eat sandwiches, browse for We love Jesus and BBQ too T-shirts, or try to win a hunting blind at bingo, they also encounter candidates of all parties, who share one outdoor stage and are given only a few minutes to address a rowdy, heckling crowd. This year, however, Fancy Farm was most remarkable for who did not show up: Mitch McConnell. Now in his 42nd and final year as a senator, the Republican has been a fixture of the event, attending 30 times . As GOP leader in the Senate for 18 years, McConnell became famous for his bare-knuckled, Machiavellian approach to politics—a method grounded in gradually amassing control through unflashy strategy and exploiting leverage for partisan ends. No man has so thoroughly thwarted Democratic ambitions, which he did both by championing the filibuster and by securing a conservative supermajority on the Supreme Court. Despite the longtime Senate leader’s absence from Fancy Farm, the specter of McConnellism hung over the event. And it will hang over America for years, too. On June 14, McConnell, who is not running for reelection, was hospitalized, taken by ambulance after he was found unconscious at his home in Washington, D.C. The 84-year-old has not been seen in public, let alone Congress, since. The two proof-of-life photos that his staff released have only provoked feverish speculation. Onstage at Fancy Farm, Charles Booker, the Democratic nominee to replace the senator, invoked Carmen Sandiego. “Where in the world is Mitch McConnell?” Booker asked. “What is going on with Mitch McConnell?” Supportive Democrats broke out in sporadic chants of “Where’s Mitch?” [ Mark Leibovich: Mitch McConnell and the president he calls ‘despicable’ ] Kentucky’s Democratic governor, Andy Beshear, a potential presidential contender, has not shied away from stirring up suspicion. Late last month, he sent a letter urging McConnell “to directly and verbally address the people of Kentucky and provide proof of your capacity to serve, or resign.” The implication has been that the master Republican tactician may be incapacitated, perhaps even deceased, but left instructions to hide this fact until after August 3—at which point Beshear would have severe difficulties installing a replacement. (Beshear has insisted that this deadline, now passed, has “no legal impact.”) Even in the twilight of McConnell’s influence, Democrats feared that he was capable of one last great trick. On Thursday, however, McConnell announced that he had been discharged from a rehabilitation center and would be working from home. The explanation for his absence turned out not to involve any convoluted conspiracy. McConnell had suffered a serious fall, just as he has in the past, and contracted pneumonia. In 2023, a similar incident resulted in a concussion and a fractured rib. Then, too, his office released only sparse and cryptic details about his condition. Eventually, McConnell returned to work and to doing what he did best: stymying the Democrats. R ecently I asked the reporter Al Cross, considered the dean of Kentucky journalism, whether McConnell had anything that could be called an ideology, or whether he was merely interested in amassing power. Without hesitating, Cross answered, “The second.” He noted that McConnell and his first wife, a feminist scholar, had had a pet named Rocky, after Nelson Rockefeller—a hero of the GOP’s now-extinct liberal wing. “He was a Rockefeller Republican,” Cross told me. “And only when the party began moving to the right did he move to the right, because he wanted to be a leader in the party. You know, this is a guy who never wanted to be anything but a politician.” McConnell’s greatest personal policy commitment seems to have been to deregulate campaign finance, which the Supreme Court eventually delivered. What most earned him both his power and the disdain of Democrats was his devotion to party above all else. The GOP for which McConnell tirelessly worked is now firmly in the hands of Donald Trump, a man whom McConnell deeply detests and yet whose ascent he has repeatedly enabled. Had McConnell not held open a Supreme Court seat after the 2016 death of Antonin Scalia, perhaps Trump would not have gained enough support from anti-abortion voters to win that year’s presidential election. Had McConnell tried to whip votes in favor of Trump’s conviction after his supporters attacked the Capitol on January 6, 2021, perhaps the party could have exorcised him. McConnell got what he wished for—the first line of his obituary will note that he was the longest-serving party leader in Senate history—but at what cost? He and the president are intertwined in history, Scott Jennings, a former McConnell strategist turned prominent Trump defender, told me. “Twenty, 50, or 100 years from now, what will be remembered most about the era and their time together is that McConnell and his political decisions enabled Trump to win the presidency, change the Supreme Court, cut taxes, and, frankly, take a pretty firm hand on international matters,” Jennings said. McConnell did not just shatter political norms by depriving Barack Obama’s Supreme Court nominee of a hearing in 2016. He also pushed through Trump’s nominees and, more than any other person, influenced the selection of appellate judges who will shape America for decades. His influence over the political system will persist in other, subtler ways. “McConnell’s people were superb at taking young Republicans under their wings and nurturing them,” Stephen Voss, a political scientist at the University of Kentucky, told me. “And those folks are spread out all over the state and also Washington, D.C.” In his home state, McConnell commands respect. He routed huge sums of federal money to Kentucky—$65 billion, by some estimates. He personally remade state politics. McConnell also regularly intervened in local elections, from the state legislature all the way down to county clerks. Democrats dominated the state when he started his career; today, they are largely shut out of power. Beshear won the governorship only to have his vetoes routinely overturned by a Republican supermajority in the state legislature. “It’s a Mitch McConnell–constructed party, even if some of the people at the grassroots don’t like him. It’s impossible to deny that he is the architect of it,” Tres Watson, a Republican strategist, told me. That is why the state GOP headquarters, in Frankfort, carries his name. O ne week after the November 2024 election, which returned Trump to the White House, I watched McConnell receive the Irving Kristol Award from the American Enterprise Institute. Robert Doar, AEI’s president, asked McConnell if he had any regrets . “Yeah, but I’m not going to tell you,” he replied. Despite stating in 2021 that Trump was “practically and morally responsible” for his supporters’ attack on the Capitol, McConnell said that he could not vote to convict the president in an impeachment trial, because Trump’s term had expired. Cross told me that, during that period, McConnell was convinced that Trump was doomed in the party. McConnell told Michael Tackett, his biographer, that his position differed from that of Liz Cheney—who sacrificed a promising career leading Republicans in the House of Representatives—because “I didn’t see how blowing yourself up and taking yourself off the playing field was helpful to getting the party back to where she and I probably both think it ought to be.” After the trial, McConnell and Trump did not speak again for almost four years. McConnell gave up his leadership role right as Trump returned to power. In his final Senate term, in which he returned to being a legislative backbencher, McConnell lodged his protests against Trump by voting against several of his nominees (Tulsi Gabbard, Pete Hegseth, Robert F. Kennedy Jr.) and strongly supporting Ukraine and free trade. [ David A. Graham: Mike Johnson would prefer not to ] At Fancy Farm, McConnell’s fellow Republicans largely papered over the schism between the biggest figure in national politics and the biggest figure in state politics. In a mark of how important McConnell has been in fostering Republicans in the state, the primary race to succeed him was between three Republicans who had all worked for him previously. Nate Morris, a man who once interned for him and then made his fortune by founding a trash-and-recycling company, tried to win by repudiating him. He released an ad showing himself riding a garbage truck saying that he was a “Trump ‘America First’ conservative” who was here “to take out the trash” by dumping McConnell. This strategy did not succeed; before the primary could occur, Morris was whisked away by Trump for the prestigious post of ambassador to Colombia. Instead the victory went to Andy Barr, a McConnellite congressman from Lexington. When I asked him what McConnell’s legacy would be, he cited three things: building up the GOP in Kentucky, “opposing unconstitutional restrictions on political speech,” and “working with President Trump to deliver a conservative supermajority on the U.S. Supreme Court and a conservative, originalist federal judiciary.” For the country as a whole, though, what McConnell’s many political victories leave behind is more dismal. His lasting contribution to the Senate is its calcification. Few people understood leverage and Senate procedure as well as McConnell; the routine use of the filibuster (which Democrats are also guilty of) has now set a precedent in which the party in power can confirm judges and pass tax bills but struggles to accomplish much else. The lack of a functional Congress has hastened the executive branch’s arrogation of the legislature’s previous responsibilities. This diminishes the separation of powers that McConnell (and his strictly constitutionalist judges) claim to be upholding. The negative consequences for Republicans may become apparent only when Democrats have a turn at power in McConnell’s beloved chamber. Because of his specific decisions—to hold open a Supreme Court seat on the theory that it was too close to an election in 2016, before doing the exact opposite in 2020—it is now inconceivable that a Democratic-led Senate would confirm another Trump justice if a vacancy arose. McConnell’s political career is ending, but his legacy will last much longer. Unfortunately, it has left America much harder to govern.

items.title: Ipres : 174 milliards FCFA de cotisations à encaisser en 2026
items.description: Le montant des cotisations à encaisser par l’Institut de prévoyance retraite du Sénégal (Ipres) est attendu à 174 milliards FCFA en 2026, soit une hausse de 7,2 milliards FCFA. C’est ce qui ressort du Document de programmation budgétaire et économique pluriannuelle (DPBEP) 2027-2029 rendu public cette semaine par le ministère de l’Économie, des Finances et du Plan. Chargée de la gestion du Régime général de retraite (RGR) et du Régime complémentaire des Cadres (RCC), en application des dispositions de la loi nᵒ 75-50 du 3 avril 1975 relative aux institutions de prévoyance sociale, l’Institution de prévoyance retraite du Sénégal (Ipres) fait face à des contraintes liées notamment au recouvrement des cotisations. En fait, selon le Document de programmation budgétaire et économique pluriannuelle (DPBEP) 2027-2029, les principales contraintes identifiées ont trait à la couverture du secteur informel. L’IPRES ne parvient toujours pas à couvrir le secteur informel. Sur ce, il est relevé dans le document que l’évasion sociale est estimée à plus de 50 % des travailleurs relevant du droit privé du travail alors que la pérennité du système de retraite repose sur le rapport démographique actifs/retraités qui était de quatre pour un dans les années 70, à deux pour un actuellement. Concernant le financement de la pension minimale, depuis l’instauration de la pension minimale qui a favorisé des droits gratuits attribués à hauteur d’environ 22,8 millions de points supplémentaires, selon la même source, la contribution de l’État n’a pas évolué au même rythme que les charges générées. A lire aussi : Prévoyance retraite : les charges de l’Ipres estimées à plus de 153 milliards de FCFA en 2024 « Néanmoins, l’Ipres continue d’assurer le paiement de ladite pension minimale dont le cumul est estimé à 30 milliards en 2026 ; l’impossibilité de mobiliser le compte de dépôt du Trésor public à souhait : le solde du compte de dépôt avoisine 50 milliards FCFA mais difficilement mobilisable, ce qui pousse l’IPRES à la titrisation moyennant un pourcentage de décote », lit-on dans le document. En réalité, il est noté un problème de recouvrement des cotisations sociales des entreprises publiques et parapubliques du fait de leurs immunités d’exécution. D’après le DPBEP 2027-2029, les entreprises publiques et parapubliques accumulent beaucoup de retards de paiements des cotisations sociales dues, privant l’institution de ressources nécessaires pour payer les pensions de retraite. « La dette de ces entreprises publiques, estimée à plus de 26 milliards FCFA en 2024, reste difficilement recouvrable à cause de l’immunité d’exécution dont elles jouissent, plombant ainsi les différents moyens de recouvrement dont dispose l’institution », souligne le texte. Par rapport à la titularisation massive des agents non-fonctionnaires et à l'érection de la fonction publique locale, le document informe que la titularisation des agents non-fonctionnaires de l’État risque de peser sur les cotisations de l’IPRES. Car le transfert de certains salariés au Fonds national de retraite (FNR), risque de fragiliser l’institution en l’absence de mesures d’encadrement. « Avec un objectif de recouvrement d’au moins 88 % sur les produits techniques, le montant des cotisations à encaisser est attendu à 174 milliards FCFA en 2026, soit une hausse de 7,2 milliards FCFA », signale le document. Il urge aussi de souligner que l’Ipres assure le recouvrement des cotisations, le paiement des prestations, la gestion financière des placements ainsi que des services médico-sociaux. Son financement repose sur une double cotisation, 60 % patronale et 40 % salariale, appliquée sur les salaires bruts plafonnés. Mariama DIEME

items.title: Sissili/Orpaillage : Le gouverneur du Nando engage le processus de formalisation du site artisanal de Sao/Lama dans la commune de Silly
items.description: Sissili/Orpaillage : Le gouverneur du Nando engage le processus de formalisation du site artisanal de Sao/Lama dans la commune de Silly Silly, 7 août 2026 (AIB) – Une délégation régionale conduite par le gouverneur de la région de Nando, le camarade Adama Jean Yves Béré, a effectué ce jeudi 7 août 2026, une mission de prospection et de sensibilisation sur le site d’exploitation artisanale d’or de Sao/Lama dans la commune de Silly. L’objectif est de toucher du doigt les réalités du terrain et d’engager le processus de formalisation du site. Arrivée sur les lieux dans l’après-midi, la mission, composée notamment du Haut-Commissaire de la province de la Sissili, le camarade Téwindé Isaac Sia, ainsi que le Président de la Délégation Spéciale (PDS) de Silly, le camarade Christophe Bonkoungou, visait à constater l’impact de l’occupation minière et à échanger directement avec les exploitants artisanaux de l’or. Prenant la parole, le gouverneur de la région du Nando, le camarade Adama Jean Yves Béré, a d’abord exprimé sa gratitude pour l’accueil qui lui a été réservé avant de retracer l’historique de ces sites. Il a souligné la nécessité de concilier l’activité minière et la préservation du Chantier d’Aménagement Forestier (CAF). « Je ressors satisfait parce que les uns et les autres ont montré une prédisposition d’esprit pour accompagner le processus qui va aboutir à la formalisation du site », a déclaré le gouverneur, tout en saluant la clairvoyance et la disponibilité des autorités locales ainsi que des orpailleurs de Sao/Lama. Sur le plan économique, le Directeur régional de l’Énergie, des Mines et des Carrières de Nando, le camarade Éric Béré, a qualifié les sites de « très potentiels », soulignant qu’ils constituent un levier de développement socio-économique majeur pour les villages riverains, la commune et le pays. Il a toutefois rappelé les impératifs écologiques liés à cette activité. « C’est une condition sine qua non pour les orpailleurs de garantir la protection de l’environnement, sans laquelle la formalisation ne peut voir le jour ». Abondant dans le même sens, le Directeur régional des Eaux et Forêts de Nando, le camarade Louis Nébié, s’est voulu rassurant quant à la prise en compte des contraintes environnementales. Il a indiqué que les études à venir permettront de prendre les dispositions requises pour minimiser l’impact sur le milieu naturel, rappelant que « ce Chantier d’Aménagement Forestier est aussi une source de revenus pour les populations riveraines ». Pour leur part, le Président de la Délégation Spéciale de Silly, Christophe Bonkoungou, et les représentants des orpailleurs ont exprimé leur vive satisfaction face à cette visite de terrain effectuée malgré les contraintes de la saison hivernale, traduisant ainsi l’intérêt porté par les autorités régionales à leurs préoccupations. Agence d’Information du Burkina LTS/ban/ata

items.title: District police commanders have made arrests over insults an ‘enterprise’ – Miracles Aboagye alleges
items.description: Aspiring National Communications Officer of the New Patriotic Party (NPP), Dennis Miracles Aboagye, has alleged that the government is presiding over a growing pattern of arrests linked to alleged insults, claiming the practice has spread from social media platforms to community-level radio and information-centre discussions. Speaking on JoyNews’ Newsfile on Saturday, Mr Aboagye said the number of people allegedly arrested over insulting comments was far greater than the public might realise. “The number of people this government has arrested because of insult, you have no idea,” he said. He claimed the NPP had been providing support to individuals affected by such cases and therefore had access to what he described as a list of people who had been arrested. “We are the ones who provide them with support, so we have the list,” he added. According to Mr Aboagye, some of the alleged arrests involve social media users, particularly TikTokers. “Most of the TikTokers’ issue, you haven’t heard,” he said. Mr Aboagye further alleged that the practice of arresting people over insulting comments has now reached the district level. He claimed some district police commanders were allegedly targeting citizens who participate in community information-centre programmes and community radio discussions. “In fact now, at the district level, the district police commanders have also made it an enterprise,” he alleged. He claimed that individuals could be arrested after speaking during such engagements. “No, you speak, they pick you up from the community, they put you in and they tell you, ‘You know, when this is taken to court, you would be jailed?’” he said. Mr Aboagye described the alleged practice as having become an “enterprise”, suggesting that arrests were no longer isolated incidents but part of a wider pattern. Mr Aboagye stated that he does not personally condone insulting behaviour. He said his Christian faith and experience as a Sunday school teacher had shaped his attitude towards abusive language. “I am a Methodist, I have been a Sunday school teacher for a very long time, I abhor insults,” he said. He also invoked his upbringing, describing himself as a “pure thoroughbred Akuapim boy” who does not engage in insults. “I don’t insult,” he stressed. Nevertheless, Mr Aboagye argued that his opposition to insulting language should not be confused with support for criminalising insults. “But insult is not a crime,” he stated. Mr Aboagye’s allegations come in the wake of the NPP’s major demonstration in Accra on Thursday. Thousands of party members, supporters and leaders took to the streets for a protest dubbed “Democracy Under Attack” , accusing the governing National Democratic Congress (NDC) of undermining Ghana’s democratic principles and weakening key state institutions. The demonstration formed part of the opposition party’s broader campaign against what it describes as threats to democratic governance, institutional independence and the rule of law. The protesters also raised concerns about the use of state institutions and what they regard as the selective application of state power. At the conclusion of the demonstration, NPP leaders presented a petition at the forecourt of Jubilee House, the seat of Ghana’s presidency. The party was represented by Minority Leader Alexander Afenyo-Markin, General Secretary Osei Kyei-Mensah-Bonsu and the Chief of Staff to NPP flagbearer Dr Mahamudu Bawumia. The NPP had earlier submitted a separate petition to the Supreme Court.

items.title: ROAD TO LA28: Ghana Para Powerlifters head to Russia as ‘Target the Podium’ initiative gains momentum
items.description: Ghana’s journey towards the Los Angeles 2028 Paralympic Games has taken another major step as the national Para Powerlifting Team competes at the 2026 International Para Powerlifting Competition in Russia. The five-member Team Ghana delegation comprises three para-powerlifting athletes – Francis Kwaku, Nfodzo Patrick and Obeng Samuel – together with Lead Coach Toulassi Frank and Assistant Coach Oheneadu George. The team’s participation forms part of the National Paralympic Committee of Ghana’s ambitious ‘Target the Podium’ Initiative, a strategic programme focused on preparing Ghanaian para-athletes for high-level international competition and ultimately the LA28 Paralympic Games. Driven by the leadership of NPC Ghana President Samson Deen, Target the Podium has one clear objective: to build Ghanaian para-athletes with the international experience, confidence, technical preparation and medal-winning mentality required to challenge for the Paralympic podium. Ghana’s participation is being supported by the National Paralympic Committee of Ghana in partnership with the Russian Paralympic Committee, providing another important international platform for the athletes to test themselves against strong opposition and continue their development towards Los Angeles 2028. The competition takes place from 8-9 August 2026, with the Ghanaian delegation scheduled to depart Russia on 10 August. President Samson Deen, in a message delivered to the athletes through their coaching team ahead of the competition, urged them to understand the bigger national mission behind their journey. “Our objective is to continue creating opportunities for our para-athletes to compete internationally, develop their confidence and gain the experience required to represent Ghana successfully on the world stage. “Los Angeles 2028 remains an important target, and every quality international competition forms part of that development journey.” For Francis Kwaku, Nfodzo Patrick and Obeng Samuel, every lift in Russia represents another opportunity to gain valuable international experience, measure their progress against international opposition and strengthen their competitive mentality. For Lead Coach Toulassi Frank and Assistant Coach Oheneadu George, the competition provides an equally important opportunity to assess the athletes under international competitive conditions and identify areas for further technical improvement as Ghana intensifies preparations towards LA28.

items.title: Gnagna : les acteurs locaux appelés à s’impliquer pour interrompre la transmission de la rougeole
items.description: Gnagna : les acteurs locaux appelés à s'impliquer pour interrompre la transmission de la rougeole Bogandé, 7 août 2026 (AIB)-Le secrétaire général de la province de la Gnagna, Mendien dit Moussa Soma, a présidé, le jeudi 6 août 2026 au Haut-commissariat de Bogandé, une rencontre de plaidoyer en faveur de la campagne nationale de vaccination contre la rougeole et la rubéole, lancée dans le district sanitaire de Bogandé. La rencontre a réuni les acteurs de la santé ainsi que plusieurs autorités et leaders locaux, en vue de renforcer leur engagement dans la mobilisation des populations pour la réussite de cette campagne. Selon les données présentées par le district sanitaire de Bogandé, la province fait face depuis plusieurs années à une circulation continue du virus de la rougeole, marquée par des flambées successives. Des foyers importants ont notamment été enregistrés dans la ville de Bogandé en 2023, à Piéla en 2024-2025 et dans la zone Est en 2025-2026. La situation demeure préoccupante en 2026, avec 998 cas de rougeole enregistrés, contre 835 en 2025, selon les données présentées au cours de la rencontre. Les moins de 15 ans représentent 74 % des cas recensés. Face à cette situation, plusieurs actions ont déjà été menées, notamment la sensibilisation des populations, la prise en charge des cas dans les formations sanitaires, deux campagnes de vaccination réactive ciblant les enfants de 9 à 59 mois, ainsi que le renforcement de la surveillance épidémiologique. Présidant la rencontre, le secrétaire général de la province de la Gnagna, Mendien dit Moussa Soma, a appelé les différents acteurs à s'impliquer davantage dans la sensibilisation et la mobilisation des communautés. Il a insisté sur la nécessité d'une conjugaison des efforts pour favoriser l'adhésion des populations à la campagne. Le médecin-chef du district sanitaire de Bogandé, Dr Moussa Sawadogo, a pour sa part présenté la situation épidémiologique et les principaux enjeux de la campagne. Il a expliqué que l'objectif est d'interrompre la transmission de la rougeole en protégeant les enfants les plus exposés grâce à une vaccination de masse. La campagne cible tous les enfants âgés de 6 mois à 10 ans, qu'ils soient déjà vaccinés ou non. La vaccination est gratuite et se déroule dans les formations sanitaires ainsi que sur des sites avancés installés dans les secteurs et villages afin de rapprocher les services des populations. Elle est prévue du 6 au 12 août 2026. Dr Moussa Sawadogo a appelé les autorités administratives, coutumières et religieuses, les leaders communautaires ainsi que les différents relais d'information à jouer pleinement leur rôle dans la mobilisation des parents. Pour lui, l'implication de ces acteurs est essentielle pour rassurer les familles sur la sécurité et l'efficacité du vaccin, combattre les rumeurs et faciliter l'accès des équipes de vaccination aux différentes localités. La campagne fait toutefois face à plusieurs défis, notamment les difficultés d'accès à certaines populations vivant dans des zones à défi sécuritaire, la circulation de rumeurs et de fausses informations sur les vaccins, l'hésitation ou le refus de certains parents, ainsi que la mobilisation des enfants dans les villages éloignés. Les acteurs ont ainsi été invités à relayer les messages de sensibilisation, à encourager tous les parents d'enfants âgés de 6 mois à 10 ans à les faire vacciner et à faciliter le travail des équipes sur le terrain. Le plaidoyer porte également sur la mobilisation de moyens financiers et logistiques, notamment des motos, des véhicules et du carburant, au profit des structures de santé. Pour les organisateurs, une communication efficace demeure déterminante pour atteindre toutes les cibles. Elle doit s'appuyer sur les canaux pertinents, diffuser des messages précis et convaincants et développer des stratégies adaptées aux zones urbaines, périurbaines, aux sites de personnes déplacées internes ainsi qu'aux zones difficiles d'accès et à défi sécuritaire. À travers cette campagne, le district sanitaire de Bogandé entend saisir l'opportunité de renforcer la protection des enfants et d'interrompre durablement la transmission de la rougeole. Pour les acteurs de santé, la réussite de l'opération repose sur l'engagement collectif des autorités, des leaders communautaires, des partenaires, des agents de santé et des populations. Agence d'information du Burkina

items.description: ICT coordinators from districts across the Greater Accra Region have undergone a two-day Advanced Digital Skills Training aimed at strengthening their capacity to support digital education in schools. The training, which opened on Thursday, August 6, and ended on Friday August 7, at the Methodist University was organised by the UNIWIZ Foundation in partnership with the Ghana Education Service (GES), ModePlus Innovation Hub and Intellite IT Solutions, with support from the Embassy of Switzerland in Ghana. The programme brought together ICT coordinators from across the region and selected ICT teachers from senior high schools for practical sessions focused on strengthening their digital skills and the use of technology in teaching and learning. The Founder and Chief Executive Officer of the UNIWIZ Foundation, Wisdom Larry Quarme-Doe, said the training forms part of efforts to strengthen the capacity of educators alongside the provision of ICT facilities in schools. items.title: Prof Bokpin cautions NPP, NDC against undermining democratic institutions
items.description: Economist and Professor of Finance, Prof. Godfred Bokpin, has cautioned Ghana’s two major political parties against allowing partisan political strategies to undermine critical institutions that underpin the country’s democracy. He said while the governing National Democratic Congress (NDC) and the opposition New Patriotic Party (NPP) may adopt different positions depending on whether they are in power or opposition, their arguments could contain elements of truth that deserve serious consideration. Prof. Bokpin made the comments while speaking on JoyNews’ Newsfile on Saturday, following the NPP’s “Democracy Under Attack” demonstration in Accra. Thousands of NPP members and supporters took to the streets of the capital on Thursday to protest what the party described as threats to Ghana’s democracy and the weakening of key state institutions. The demonstration culminated in the presentation of a petition at the forecourt of Jubilee House, with the party’s delegation led by Minority Leader Alexander Afenyo-Markin, General Secretary Osei Kyei-Mensah-Bonsu and the Chief of Staff to NPP flagbearer Dr Mahamudu Bawumia. The party had earlier submitted a separate petition to the Supreme Court. Prof. Bokpin urged Ghanaians to look beyond the immediate political contest and consider whether recurring claims by both major parties point to deeper institutional problems. “I do not think that these two main political parties would fake a position depending on where they find themselves,” he said. “Perhaps, there is an element of truth in what they are capable of doing when they are in power, for which reason they see certain outcomes in a certain way.” Prof. Bokpin suggested that if the concerns raised by the two parties are genuine, the country must find a way to address them rather than allowing them to become recurring features of Ghana’s political discourse. “But if that is not the case, then we need to find a solution to it because, to some extent, it is gaining attraction,” he said. Rather than dismissing such accusations as mere political rhetoric, Prof. Bokpin said there may be substantive issues that require attention. Prof. Bokpin also drew attention to the significant number of people who participated in the NPP demonstration. He acknowledged that the turnout demonstrated that the issues being raised had gained traction among a section of the population, while also recognising the political calculations that often accompany opposition demonstrations. “If you look at the number of people who joined the demonstration,” he said. However, he noted that demonstrations could also serve as part of an opposition party’s broader political strategy. “It is also the case of a political strategy,” he said. “When you are in opposition, you want to do this consistently and all of that just to make the government look some way and all of that.” Despite recognising the political dimension of the demonstration, Prof. Bokpin warned that political actors must be careful not to weaken the very institutions that sustain Ghana’s democracy. “But I think that we should just be mindful that through these actions we may be undermining critical institutions that underpin our democracy,” he said. Prof. Bokpin also expressed concern about the impact of political disputes on public perceptions of the judiciary. He specifically referred to “how we see judges in this country”, highlighting the importance of maintaining confidence in the judicial system.

items.title: Government must not burst the bubble of democratic freedoms – Miracles Aboagye
items.description: Aspiring National Communications Officer of the New Patriotic Party (NPP), Dennis Miracles Aboagye, has cautioned the government against actions that could undermine democratic freedoms, particularly the right of citizens to freely express their views. According to him, one of the most important safeguards of democracy is the ability of citizens to protest, criticise those in power and demand accountability without fear of intimidation. Speaking in an interview on JoyNews’ Newsfile on Saturday on the recent ‘Democracy Under Attack demonstration, Mr Aboagye described protests as a powerful tool that can help governments break out of what he called a “bubble” created by the trappings of political power. “Sometimes when you are in government, and we will be in there, you find yourself in a bubble. If you don’t take care, you will see things only as they appear to you where you are,” he said. He explained that demonstrations and public dissent can serve as a reality check for governments by exposing concerns that may not be visible from within government. “Protest sometimes pokes this bubble, bursts it, and then you feel a certain new air, and you decide what to do,” he added. Mr Aboagye said governments often find it easy to justify their decisions while in power, but warned that such approaches are rarely sustainable when they fail to respond to legitimate public concerns. He, however, said the broader democratic implications of the demonstration should receive greater attention than the immediate political disagreements surrounding it. According to him, the arrest and prosecution of citizens over comments made on social media raise serious questions about the state of freedom of expression in Ghana. Using the case of a woman who allegedly expressed her views on TikTok, Mr Aboagye said the incident demonstrates how ordinary citizens are increasingly using digital platforms to participate in democratic discourse. He noted that many citizens do not have access to mainstream media platforms such as Newsfile, Asɛmpa or Joy FM, making social media their primary avenue for expressing their views on national issues. “This woman goes to sleep. 5 a.m., her room is broken into by security services. She is put into an Elx vehicle, drove on the road for eight hours to Accra, sent to a court, and she is remanded for two weeks,” he said. He questioned the justification for such an arrest, particularly where the police subsequently indicated that the woman had been arrested for allegedly insulting a government official. “For me, that is the biggest issue to look at. Forget about the police car clash. As for the police car clash, we have our own games that we play. Let’s not use that to cloud the very important underlying issue with democracy,” Mr Aboagye stressed. He argued that the incident should prompt a wider national conversation about the limits of state power and the protection of citizens’ constitutional freedoms. Mr Aboagye maintained that democratic governments must be prepared to tolerate criticism, including criticism expressed through new and sometimes unconventional platforms such as TikTok. He said protecting the right of citizens to express themselves is essential to maintaining public confidence in Ghana’s democratic system.

items.title: Tapoa : Le président de la délégation spéciale de Diapaga au contact des producteurs de la commune
items.description: Tapoa : Le président de la délégation spéciale de Diapaga au contact des producteurs de la commune Diapaga, 5 août 2026 (AIB)-Le président de la délégation spéciale de Diapaga, Yambi Bamogo, a mis à profit la fête de l'indépendance pour visiter les champs et échanger avec les producteurs de sa commune. Il était accompagné dans cette sortie par le 1er vice-président Soali Ouali. Le déplacement qui l'a conduit sur le site rizicole de la commune où 306 ménages exploitent le riz sur une superficie de 10 hectares. Ce site, il faut le rappeler, a été aménagé par l'ONG Action contre la Faim en 2025, au profit des personnes affectées par le terrorisme dans la commune de Diapaga. La province de la Tapoa fait face depuis quelques années à des défis sécuritaires et humanitaires. C'est donc pour inverser la tendance et s'inscrire dans la dynamique nationale de relèvement et de résilience des communautés, conformément aux orientations du camarade Président du Faso, le Capitaine Ibrahim Traoré, qui appelle les Burkinabè à produire ce qu'ils consomment et à consommer ce qu'ils produisent, que la délégation spéciale a élaboré ce projet avec la bénédiction financière de l'ACF, afin que les déplacés internes et les hôtes de Diapaga puissent retrouver leur autonomie alimentaire et sortir progressivement de la logique d'assistanat. 10,30 hectares, dont 404 parcelles de 250 m² chacune, fruits du partenariat entre la délégation spéciale et l'ACF, ont ainsi été aménagés pour 306 ménages bénéficiaires. Les producteurs bénéficient d'intrants, de semences améliorées, de deux châteaux d'eau, et de l'accompagnement technique du service de l'agriculture. Au cours de la visite, le président de la délégation spéciale, Yambi Bamogo, a salué l'engagement de l'ACF et encouragé les producteurs à travailler avec abnégation. Il a déclaré : « Le riz que vous produisez ici est la preuve que même dans la difficulté, nous pouvons nous prendre en charge. » Du site rizicole aux champs de maïs, les spéculations sont au stade de ramification et montaison pour certains, et à celui d'épiaison pour le maïs. Toutes les spéculations présentent une physionomie qui augure de bonnes récoltes si les pluies se poursuivent. Pour Bakari Kaboré, chef de zone d'agriculture, l'impact attendu est de 5 à 6 tonnes par hectare de riz sur le site, ce qui va réduire la dépendance à l'aide. Et le PDS de conclure que le travail abattu sur le site est un message clair : la commune de Diapaga refuse de tendre la main, et la souveraineté alimentaire est en marche dans sa commune. Possibo Couldiati, une exploitante sur le site rizicole : « On n'attendait des sacs de riz d'ailleurs. Aujourd'hui, c'est nous qui produisons notre propre riz. C'est une fierté pour nous. » Il faut noter que 20 bassins sont prévus pour le maraîchage en saison sèche. La spéculation utilisée est la FKR 19. Agence d'Information du Burkina LBK/ata

items.title: Impact des feux de brousse au Sénégal : 499 milliards de FCFA de pertes économiques notées en terme de fourrages
items.description: Les pertes économiques en termes de fourrages durant la campagne 2024-2025 sont estimées à 499 milliards FCFA à cause de la biomasse herbacée brûlée. C’est ce que relève le Document de programmation budgétaire et économique pluriannuelle (DPBEP) 2027-2029. Les feux de brousse sont des facteurs anthropiques de dégradation de la biodiversité. Ils entraînent des conséquences économiques et sociales drastiques. Ils occasionnent aussi un dérèglement des équilibres écologiques et une dégradation des sols. « Les pertes économiques en termes de fourrages durant la campagne 2024-2025 sont estimées à 499 milliards FCFA à cause de la biomasse herbacée brûlée. L’ampleur du phénomène justifie l’importance du budget alloué à la campagne 2026-2027 estimé à 645 000 000 FCFA », renseigne le Document de programmation budgétaire et économique pluriannuelle (DPBEP) 2027-2029. De manière générale, la même source indique qu’au-delà des feux de brousse, la recrudescence des phénomènes climatiques extrêmes comme les inondations reste un défi assez préoccupant au Sénégal. À la lecture de leurs incidences sur les finances publiques, ces inondations représentent un facteur de risque budgétaire majeur en termes de coût économique. En fait, 70 % des dommages totaux sont relatifs aux inondations. Cette situation est exacerbée, selon le document, par une pluviométrie de plus en plus dévastatrice et une urbanisation spontanée et mal maîtrisée, exposant ainsi les populations et leurs biens. 3,507 milliards FCFA de dommages moyens annuels causés par les inondations « Ainsi, en 2025, des débordements de cours d’eau le long du fleuve Sénégal (entre Kidira et Matam) et du fleuve Gambie (Kédougou) ont rendu vulnérables beaucoup d’espaces socialisés. Par exemple, pour le bassin versant du Lac Rose, que le nombre moyen annuel (NMA) de personnes exposées aux inondations par ruissellement est estimé à environ 3 500 personnes, tandis que les dommages moyens annuels s’élèvent à 3,507 milliards FCFA », lit-on dans le document. Aussi, les bâtiments résidentiels représentent plus de 2,78 milliards FCFA de pertes annuelles. En somme, les inondations affectent plusieurs secteurs productifs, diminuent les recettes fiscales, ralentissent la croissance économique et réduisent les marges budgétaires. En 2025, la mise en place de la Stratégie nationale de gestion du risque d’inondation (SNGRI) postule pour une gestion-prévention des inondations de 7 sites. Il s’agit de Bambilor et Sangalkam, Lac Rose, Touba, Kaffrine, Kaolack, Tamba et Kédougou. A lire aussi : DPBEP 2027- 2029 : une consolidation budgétaire résolue, sans austérité Sur les épidémies et autres urgences sanitaires, il est souligné dans le DPBEP qu’il s’agit de risques dont la survenance est imprévisible. La gestion de ces risques est fonction de la capacité de réponse de l’État, de l’exigence de célérité dans les interventions et de la mobilisation des ressources pour contenir leurs impacts négatifs. « A cet effet, un dispositif de surveillance des maladies épidémiques est mis en place à travers le Comité national de gestion des épidémies. La dotation budgétaire de 59 982 000 FCFA allouée en 2026 au centre des opérations d’urgence sanitaire justifie la maîtrise des menaces externes récurrentes », révèle le document. Par ailleurs, l’intervention des services d’hygiène, le renforcement de la recherche épidémiologique (100 000 000 FCFA en 2026 pour IRESSEF) et la prise en charge des maladies chroniques non transmissibles (470 000 000 FCFA) confortent la gestion efficiente de ces risques d’urgences sanitaires. Mariama DIEME

items.title: Gayéri : les orpailleurs offrent 825 000 FCFA en soutien aux VDP
items.description: Gayéri : les orpailleurs offrent 825 000 FCFA en soutien aux VDP Gayéri, 7 août 2026 (AIB)-L'Union des orpailleurs de la Komondjari a remis, vendredi à Gayéri, une contribution de 825 000 FCFA en soutien aux Volontaires pour la défense de la patrie (VDP) de la province, dans un élan de solidarité en faveur des forces engagées pour la sécurisation du territoire. Le don a été reçu par le président de la Délégation spéciale (PDS) de la commune de Gayéri, le camarade Emmanuel Lankoandé, représentant les communes de Gayéri et de Foutouri. Selon le PDS, cette contribution constitue un nouvel acte de patriotisme et de solidarité de la part des orpailleurs de la province. Il a précisé que le montant total est réparti à raison de 625 000 FCFA au profit des VDP basés à Gayéri et de 200 000 FCFA en faveur de ceux de Tankoualou. « Les orpailleurs viennent une fois de plus de poser un geste très louable et hautement apprécié », a déclaré le camarade Emmanuel Lankoandé. Au nom des Délégations spéciales des communes de Gayéri et de Foutouri, il a exprimé sa profonde reconnaissance à l'endroit des orpailleurs pour leurs multiples actions de soutien aux efforts de sécurisation de la province. Il a également formulé des bénédictions pour la bonne marche de leurs activités, tout en les encourageant à poursuivre leur engagement citoyen au profit de la paix et de la cohésion sociale. Cette contribution s'inscrit dans la dynamique de mobilisation des forces vives de la Komondjari en faveur des VDP, engagés aux côtés des Forces de défense et de sécurité dans la lutte contre l'insécurité. Agence d'Information du Burkina LNY/Ata

items.title: NPP re-run Bantema Constituency election under tight security after annulment of initial poll
items.description: A re-run election for Bantema Constituency executives of the New Patriotic Party (NPP) is underway at the Kumasi Cultural Centre amid tight security. The exercise comes after the NPP’s National Steering Committee annulled the initial election held on Sunday, July 11, 2026. In a statement, the Committee cited breaches of party directives, election regulations and, in some cases, existing court orders as reasons for nullifying the earlier polls. Despite the National Steering Committee’s decision, JoyNews understands that the Ashanti Regional Chairman of the NPP, Bernard Antwi Boasiako, popularly known as Chairman Wontumi, sworn into office those elected during the annulled election. However, the party is insisting on a re-run. That development created tension within the constituency and raised questions about party authority and internal discipline ahead of the re-run. In contrast to the initial election, which was held without Electoral Commission oversight, the ongoing process is being supervised by officials from the Commission. A total of 1,258 delegates are expected to cast their ballots as three different voting centers have been created at the polling center to ensure the smooth conduct of the process. Party officials say the re-run is also being closely supervised by national and regional representatives to ensure strict adherence to the NPP’s constitution and electoral guidelines. Security personnel from the Ghana Police Service have been deployed to the venue to maintain law and order and prevent any possible disturbances. The process, which is scheduled to end at 4pm, will see delegates elect new constituency executives to lead the party’s activities in Bantema ahead of the 2028 general elections. The NPP leadership says it remains committed to upholding due process and ensuring unity within the party structures in the Ashanti Region. The keenly contested position is that of Chairman, between the incumbent, Fiifi Mensah and his vice, Kingsley Atta. In the annulled election, Kingsley Atta defeated the incumbent chairman, Fiifi Mensah, with 714 votes, representing 72.8% of the 995 valid votes cast. Fiifi Mensah obtained 267 votes, representing 27.2%.

items.title: How a Hong Kong charity is using AI to help migrant workers tackle exploitation

items.title: ‘Don’t weaponise the law against citizens’ – Miracles Aboagye
items.description: Dennis Miracles Aboagye, an aspiring National Communications Officer of the New Patriotic Party (NPP), has cautioned the government against what he describes as the weaponisation of the law against ordinary citizens, particularly in cases involving freedom of speech and social media activity. Speaking on JoyNews’ Newsfile on Saturday, August 8, Mr Aboagye said the government should not use arrests and prosecutions as a substitute for civic education, especially when dealing with citizens who may not fully understand the limits of their right to free expression. “What I think the government can do is to rather activate state institutions like NCCE to begin to educate these people and tell them, listen, yes, there is free speech,” he said. “But within the free speech, you can’t say A, you can’t say B, you can’t say C.” He said citizens should instead be educated on the boundaries of free speech and encouraged to express themselves responsibly. “And begin to encourage them. You don’t go rather weaponising those who take a job,” he added. Democracy and the right to protest Mr Aboagye also rejected arguments that Ghana’s democracy cannot be under threat simply because citizens have been allowed to organise and participate in demonstrations. “Democracy has several tools. Democracy has several tools. Protest is one of them,” he said. He argued that allowing demonstrations alone does not demonstrate that all democratic principles are being respected. “If you accept the principles and systems of governance and democracy, you don’t do some and leave some,” he said. “You don’t go arresting people in their bedrooms for insult and use the fact that you allow them to protest as an example of democracy.” He described such an approach as hypocritical. “Try that. You are hypocrite if you do that,” he said. Mr Aboagye maintained that democratic rights must be applied consistently, regardless of which political party is in government. A call for consistency Mr Aboagye’s central argument was that democratic principles should not be applied selectively. He said people who previously supported the targeting of political opponents should be mindful that the same practices could eventually affect ordinary citizens. The debate, he suggested, should therefore move beyond the NPP and NDC and focus on the protection of citizens, freedom of expression, the right to protest and the fair application of the law. “Forget about us,” he reiterated. “The citizens, the market women by the roadside.”

items.title: SN-BRAFASO : Le Camarade ministre PODA constate l’état des travaux du canal d’évacuation des eaux.
items.description: (Ouagadougou, 7 août 2026). Le Camarade ministre de l’Industrie, du Commerce et de l’Artisanat, Serge Gnaniodem PODA, est sur le site de la Société Nouvelle-Brasseries du Faso (SN-BRAFASO), ce vendredi, dans la commune de Komsilga. Accompagné d’une délégation, il est là pour constater de visu l’état d’avancement des travaux, notamment la qualité des infrastructures de canalisation. Au cours de cette visite, le ministre et sa délégation inspectent le canal d’évacuation des eaux, construit par la Société dans le cadre de sa responsabilité sociétale pour répondre aux besoins des riverains. Sur place, le Camarade PODA instruit les responsables techniques concernés d'opérer quelques réajustements quant aux travaux de finition du canal, avant sa réception officielle. Il insiste aussi sur le renforcement de la sécurité des riverains et surtout sur la nécessité pour l’entreprise en charge des travaux de prendre toutes les dispositions utiles pour offrir un ouvrage de qualité répondant aux orientations et aux normes. Par ailleurs, le visiteur du jour ne manque pas d’interpeller quelques riverains sur l'utilisation anarchique de l’ouvrage. Séance tenante, des instructions sont données pour déguerpir certains passages dangereux érigés déjà par certains usagers sur le canal. Avant de quitter les lieux, le Camarade ministre PODA insiste sur les travaux de finition, qui doivent prendre en compte tous les détails constatés. Pour lui, aucun manquement technique ne saurait être toléré : tout doit être parfait, au grand bonheur des riverains, condition sine qua non avant la réception officielle de l’ouvrage. DCRP Ministère du Commerce et de l'industrie.

items.title: La musique italienne en force dans les festivals d’été tunisiens
items.description: La musique italienne comme trait d’union entre les deux rives de la Méditerranée, entre tradition et modernité, grandes scènes et sites archéologiques, symboles de l’histoire partagée entre l’Europe et l’Afrique du Nord. Tel est le fil conducteur de la Semaine de la musique italienne en Tunisie, qui sera clôturée ce soir, samedi 8 août 2026, dans le cadre spectaculaire de l’amphithéâtre romain d’El Jem avec le concert «Napoli nel Mediterraneo» de l’Orchestra Instabile di Arezzo (Oida). (Photo : Concert de Rondo Veneziano à Carthage). Cette initiative, organisée dans le cadre des célébrations du 70 e anniversaire des relations diplomatiques entre l’Italie et la Tunisie, a permis de présenter, sur les principales scènes estivales du pays, différentes facettes de la musique italienne. Après l’ouverture le 2 août au Festival d’Hammamet avec Mario Biondi — l’une des voix italiennes les plus célèbres à l’international — et le concert du Rondò Veneziano le 4 août au théâtre romain de Carthage, c’est donc El Jem qui accueillera la clôture de la manifestation. Un parcours traversant des genres, des époques et des langages variés, tout en instaurant un dialogue entre la musique italienne et certains des lieux les plus emblématiques du patrimoine culturel tunisien. «Napoli nel Mediterraneo» proposera un voyage au cœur de la tradition musicale napolitaine et italienne, allant des célèbres chansons classiques napolitaines aux grands airs d’opéra, en passant par des morceaux issus de la tradition populaire. Sur la scène de l’amphithéâtre d’El Jem — l’un des monuments romains les mieux conservés au monde —, l’Orchestra Instabile d’Arezzo sera dirigé par le maestro Filippo Zambelli, avec la participation des solistes Gianni Bruschi, Loredana Carannante et Carlo Putelli. Le choix de Naples comme figure centrale de l’événement revêt une signification particulière dans le cadre d’une manifestation bâtie sur le dialogue entre les deux rives de la Méditerranée. La tradition musicale napolitaine, marquée au fil des siècles par des métissages, des échanges et des influences venus de cultures diverses, devient en effet le symbole d’un espace méditerranéen où les identités ne s’opposent pas, mais se rencontrent et se transforment. Mario Biondi à Hammamet. Des siècles de métissages culturels méditerranéens «La culture est l’un des piliers du partenariat entre l’Italie et la Tunisie. En intégrant la Semaine de la musique italienne à trois des principaux festivals tunisiens, nous célébrons non seulement le cap des 70 ans de nos relations diplomatiques, mais aussi des siècles de dialogue, d’échanges et de métissages culturels qui ont contribué à façonner nos sociétés et constituent le fondement de la relation privilégiée entre nos peuples» , a déclaré l’ambassadeur d’Italie en Tunisie, Alessandro Prunas, à la veille de l’événement. Le lien entre musique, patrimoine et diplomatie culturelle s’est également manifesté avec éclat à Carthage, où, le 4 août, le concert du Rondò Veneziano a suscité une longue et chaleureuse ovation de la part du public du théâtre romain, dans le cadre de la 60 e édition du Festival international de Carthage. La soirée a revêtu une dimension particulière grâce à la présence du maestro Gian Piero Reverberi, fondateur, compositeur et chef d’orchestre historique du Rondò Veneziano ; il est remonté exceptionnellement sur le podium pour ce qui, selon la production, constituait son ultime concert et sa dernière apparition publique. Sa participation a conféré à cet événement tunisien une valeur artistique et symbolique unique, en faisant un moment appelé à marquer l’histoire de l’ensemble. Reverberi avait mis un terme à ses activités de concertiste depuis quelques années pour des raisons de santé. Toutefois, quelques jours avant le concert de Carthage, il était remonté sur scène par surprise lors de la première date de la tournée à Bergame, dirigeant certains des derniers morceaux en rappel et recevant, là aussi, une longue ovation. Le concert «Napoli nel Mediterraneo» de l’Orchestra Instabile di Arezzo (Oida), ce samedi soir, à El Jem. Après avoir pris connaissance de la portée institutionnelle de la soirée tunisienne — inscrite parmi les initiatives de l’ambassade d’Italie et de l’Institut culturel italien pour célébrer les 70 ans de relations diplomatiques entre les deux pays —, le maestro a décidé de faire une exception et de diriger à nouveau l’orchestre. Selon la production, sa participation s’est faite à titre entièrement gracieux, comme un geste personnel témoignant de son adhésion à la valeur culturelle et symbolique de l’initiative. Le Festival international de Carthage constitue, du reste, l’un des principaux carrefours culturels de la Méditerranée. Créé en 1964, il se déroule chaque année en juillet et août dans le célèbre théâtre romain, site inscrit au patrimoine mondial de l’Unesco depuis 1979. Né à l’initiative du ministère des Affaires culturelles pour promouvoir le dialogue interculturel et valoriser le patrimoine historique national, le festival porte chaque été la musique et les arts contemporains au cœur d’un site datant de l’Antiquité. Au fil des décennies, la manifestation a progressivement renforcé sa dimension internationale, passant du statut d’événement essentiellement local à celui de rendez-vous culturel parmi les plus anciens et les plus reconnus d’Afrique du Nord et du bassin méditerranéen. C’est Mario Biondi — artiste au rayonnement international affirmé, invité à célébrer le vingtième anniversaire de ‘‘Handful of Soul’’ , l’album qui a marqué sa percée sur la scène européenne — qui a inauguré la Semaine de la musique italienne le 2 août au Festival international de Hammamet. Avec un répertoire mêlant soul et jazz, Biondi a incarné la facette la plus contemporaine de la musique italienne exportée à l'étranger, ouvrant ainsi un cycle qui a ensuite mis à l’honneur la musique orchestrale ainsi que les traditions musicales vénitienne et napolitaine. De Hammamet à Carthage, jusqu’à l’amphithéâtre d’El Jem, la Semaine de la musique italienne ne se présente pas seulement comme une série de concerts, mais comme un itinéraire culturel traversant des lieux et des langages qui témoignent de la profondeur des liens unissant l’Italie et la Tunisie. Un parcours où la musique devient un instrument de diplomatie culturelle tout en s’affirmant comme un langage universel, capable de restituer à la Méditerranée sa vocation historique d’espace de rencontre, d’échange et de métissage. D’après Agenzia Nova . L’article La musique italienne en force dans les festivals d’été tunisiens est apparu en premier sur Kapitalis .

items.title: NDC has been ‘more zealous’ in prosecuting opposition than its own – Kofi Bentil
items.description: Senior lawyer and Vice-President of IMANI Africa, Kofi Bentil, has said there are grounds for concerns that the governing National Democratic Congress (NDC) may be applying justice selectively. He argued that the government has appeared more aggressive in prosecuting opposition figures while being more lenient towards people within its own ranks. Speaking on JoyNews’ Newsfile on Saturday, Mr Bentil said both sides of the debate over selective justice could marshal arguments to support their positions, but insisted that the government’s record over its four-year mandate would ultimately provide the strongest basis for judging the allegation. “I think those arguing for selective justice will have enough facts to back what they are saying, but those who are also arguing that we don’t have selective justice will have their case too,” he said. “But the proof of the pudding is in its eating. This government and by extension this NDC party will be judged after four years.” Mr Bentil’s comments come against the backdrop of a major demonstration by the opposition New Patriotic Party (NPP) in Accra on Thursday. Thousands of NPP members and supporters took to the streets under the theme “Democracy Under Attack”, accusing the government of undermining democratic principles and weakening key state institutions. The demonstration ended with the NPP presenting a petition at the Supreme Court and the forecourt of Jubilee House, the seat of government. The delegation was led by Minority Leader Alexander Afenyo-Markin, General Secretary Osei Kyei-Mensah-Bonsu and the Chief of Staff to NPP flagbearer Dr Mahamudu Bawumia. Mr Bentil said two years into the NDC government’s four-year mandate, there was already sufficient material for citizens to begin assessing its approach to law enforcement and prosecution. “Two years have passed, if you draw the report card, there is ground to say that they have been more zealous in prosecuting people in the opposition and more zealous in freeing people from within their ranks,” he said. “And to that extent therefore, you can claim there is selective justice.” Mr Bentil’s assessment suggests that the perception is not merely about individual prosecutions but about whether there is a discernible pattern in how state power is exercised. However, he stopped short of suggesting that the debate was settled. He acknowledged that those defending the government could also point to facts and cases to support their argument that justice was not being applied selectively. Mr Bentil also explained why he believes citizens should act before democratic freedoms are seriously compromised. “For me, I am not waiting for all of our democracy to be removed from under our feet and for us to fall down before we rise up,” he said. He called for continued vigilance and active participation in the protection of civic freedoms. “So we always have to make sure that we are staying at the forefront and ensure that we expand the frontiers of freedom,” he said.

items.title: CAN 2026 féminine, Algérie – Côte-d’Ivoire : double enjeu historique pour les Fennecs
items.description: L’équipe d’Algérie affronte la Côte d’Ivoire en quarts de finale de la CAN 2026 féminine ce samedi 8 août à Rabat (18 h 00, heure algérienne), avec un double enjeu pour les Fennecs. Menées par Marine Dafeur , auteure de deux buts depuis le début de cette compétition, dont un bijou face au Kenya (2-0) lors de la dernière journée de la phase de groupe lundi 3 août, l’équipe d’Algérie vise une double qualification historique au dernier carré de la CAN 2026 et à la prochaine Coupe du monde 2027 au Brésil. Mais la tâche des Vertes ne sera pas facile face aux Ivoiriennes qui reviennent par la grande porte dans cette compétition après 12 ans d’absence. Algérie – Côte d’Ivoire : le choc des quarts de finale de la CAN 2026 Au premier tour, la Côte d’Ivoire a terminé à la première place avec sept points, sans aucune défaite. Elle a écrasé le Burkina Faso (4-1), fait match nul face à l’Afrique du Sud (2-2) et a dominé la Tanzanie (2-1). Si l’attaque ivoirienne est dangereuse avec huit buts marqués en trois matchs, sa défense a montré des signes de fébrilité, avec quatre buts encaissés. Pour l’Algérie, elle a terminé le premier tour avec un seul but encaissé face au Maroc (0-1) et son attaque a réussi à marquer quatre buts contre le Sénégal (2-0) et le Kenya (2-0). Dans ce choc, les Fennecs peuvent compter sur une défense de fer et une attaque dangereuse pour réaliser un exploit historique. Pour regarder le match en direct, il sera diffusé par beIN Sports 6. L’article CAN 2026 féminine, Algérie – Côte-d’Ivoire : double enjeu historique pour les Fennecs est apparu en premier sur TSA .

items.title: Attack on democracy creeps in, it doesn’t happen suddenly – Kofi Bentil warns
items.description: Lawyer and Vice President of IMANI Africa, Kofi Bentil, has cautioned that Ghana’s democracy can gradually deteriorate when laws are applied in ways that exceed the intentions of their framers. Speaking on JoyNews’ Newsfile on Saturday, August 8, during discussions on the New Patriotic Party’s (NPP) Democracy Under Attack demonstration, Mr Bentil said attacks on democratic systems do not necessarily occur suddenly but can develop gradually through the misuse of democratic institutions and laws. He explained that democratic freedoms must be actively protected by citizens, particularly when they believe those freedoms are being threatened. “When you talk about an attack on democracy, it never ever in the history of mankind happens suddenly. It creeps on you as a nation,” he said. Mr Bentil cited historical examples of leaders who rose to power through democratic processes but later used laws and state institutions to weaken constitutional governance. He referenced Adolf Hitler and Benito Mussolini, arguing that their experiences demonstrate how democratic principles and legal mechanisms can potentially be manipulated to undermine democracy itself. According to him, Ghana must therefore remain vigilant against practices that could gradually weaken constitutional freedoms. “We have had cause also to say, hey, the way you are applying these laws is an extension beyond which the framers of the law intended. And when you start that creep, it does not stop,” he stated. Mr Bentil also defended the role of protesters and activists in sustaining democracy, saying citizens who take to the streets to challenge leadership should be respected even when others disagree with their demands. “It is the activists you saw on the road who push the boundaries of freedom and democracy and make your liberty assured,” he said. He argued that criticism of protesters based on their past actions should not be used to deny them their democratic rights. “Even if we are wrong, even if we did something yesterday that people found to be immoral or whatever it is, it does not stop us. We don’t lose the right to say the things we are saying,” he added. Mr Bentil stressed that political leaders are accountable to citizens and should not regard themselves as rulers over the people. “We are not your subjects. You lead on our behalf,” he said, urging citizens to periodically remind leaders that political authority ultimately belongs to the people. While acknowledging that Ghana remains a free country and that the situation may not yet amount to a full-scale democratic crisis, Mr Bentil said recent concerns over the application of laws and alleged selective justice should not be dismissed. He maintained that democracy requires constant vigilance because freedoms can be lost incrementally if citizens fail to challenge actions that threaten constitutional rights.
